key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface potentials more uniform and stable, with stronger and faster-rising photovoltage response under illumination.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatments can reduce grain-boundary barriers and photovoltage losses, improving the electronic uniformity needed for more efficient, reliable perovskite solar cells.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark contact potential difference (CPD) before and after AEAPTMS passivation
Track illumination-driven surface photovoltage (SPV) dynamics and wavelength dependence; separate grain-boundary vs grain-interior signals
evidence_signal: AEAPTMS narrowed dark CPD distribution from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: The results come from thin-film nanoscale measurements, so translating the same passivation benefits into full device performance and long-term stability still needs validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
